business_rules: Users must register with a username and password; duplicate usernames are not allowed (RF-01, RF-34).
At least two user roles exist: regular user and administrator (RF-03, RNF-45).
Access is denied when the user does not exist, the password is incorrect, or the stated role does not match the registration (RF-04).
Catalog-management functions are restricted to the administrator role (RF-06, RNF-46).
A movie title is the unique identifier for catalog registration; duplicate titles are not allowed (RF-28, RF-35).
A movie must belong to at least one category and may belong to more than one category (RF-20, RNF-56).
Movie registration must include at minimum title, rating, alternate title, release date, duration, director, screenplay, cast, categories, synopsis, and poster (RF-27).
Deletion of nonexistent movies must be prevented (RF-33).
Before batch deletion, the administrator must be informed which movies have been selected (RF-32).
Playback requires the video file to be available in the delivery area; if not, the system must attempt to obtain it from the configured local repository (RF-24, RF-25).
Automatic playback depends on the existence of an MP4 file corresponding to the registered title, and the source filename must follow the expected pattern (RNF-58, RNF-59).
Uploading the video file and registering the movie are related but independent steps (RNF-57).
The catalog must be displayed in pages of up to 12 movies (RNF-40).
User, movie, and category information must be persistently stored, preserving uniqueness to prevent duplicates (RNF-42, RNF-43).
Operations must return a consistent response format with status, message, and data, and controlled error messages whenever possible (RNF-41, RNF-44).

capabilities.name: Catalog administration

capabilities.name: Registration consistency enforcement

capabilities.name: Persistent data storage

capabilities.description: Maintains a consistent response format indicating status, message, and returned data, and returns controlled error messages whenever possible.
capabilities.name: Consistent API response handling

capabilities.description: Supports large video uploads up to 2 GB, treats MP4 as the standard format, and provides a local area for temporary storage/serving and a configured local repository for on-demand loading.

capabilities.description: Allows the user interface and application services to evolve independently and for the UI to consume services even when deployed in a different environment.
